title: Lesson 1. First HTML
description:
What a website is made of, tags, page skeleton,

and style

learn.intro: Hi! Today we take our first step into the web: we'll learn what a website is made of and write our first page. Let's go!

sections.title: A website is like a person

slides.text: Imagine a website is a **person**. It has a skeleton, clothes and a brain.
**HTML** is the skeleton: the page structure is built from it. **CSS** is skin and clothes: colors, sizes, beauty. **JavaScript** is the brain: it makes the site alive.
HTML is the skeleton, CSS is the clothes, JavaScript is the brain of a website.

check.topic: What a site is made of
check.prompt: Match the language and the part of the «person»

check.topic: What a site is made of
check.prompt: CSS is responsible for how a website looks.
check.explain: CSS is the site's «clothes»: colors, fonts, sizes.

slides.text:
Code is **commands for the browser**. In HTML, commands are written with **tags** in angle brackets: `

`, ``.
A page is saved in a file with the **.html** extension. The main page of a site is usually called **index.html**.
Name the main page file index.html — the browser looks for it first.

check.prompt: What is the extension of an HTML file?
check.explain: HTML pages are saved in .html files.

check.prompt: What is the main page file usually called?

slides.text: Every page has the same skeleton: `html`, with `head` and `body` inside.
slides.code:
<html>
  <head>
    <title>My site</title>
  </head>
  <body>
    What you see goes here
  </body>
</html>

slides.text: **head** is the invisible part: service information. **body** is the visible part: everything a person sees on the page.
**title** lives inside head. Its text is shown on the **browser tab**, not on the page itself.
head — hidden, body — visible, title — the text on the tab.

check.prompt: Which tag holds everything visible on the page?
check.explain: body is the visible part of the page.

check.prompt: The text from <title> is shown on the browser tab.
check.explain: title is the text on the tab.

slides.text:
The `

` tag is a paragraph of text. It is a **paired** tag: it has an opening and a closing tag.

The closing tag is the same, just with a slash **/** before the name: `

`.

Opened a tag — don't forget to close it:

…

.

check.explain:
A closing tag has / before the name:

.

slides.text: To color text, add the **style** attribute to a tag. Inside, write a property, a colon and a value.
**color** changes the text color (red, green, blue…), and **font-size** changes the size (12px, 24px, 40px). Properties can go together, separated by **;**
Try different colors and sizes — you'll remember faster. Homework: 4–5 paragraphs about yourself, each with its own color and size.

check.prompt: Which property changes the text size?
check.explain: font-size is the font size, for example 24px.

check.prompt: In style, a colon goes between the property and the value: color: red
